one_liner: TypeScript library that predicts the browser's line breaks and paragraph heights from cached Canvas widths, so apps skip DOM reflow reads.
what_it_does: Computes how many lines a paragraph takes, and where each line breaks, at any width, without inserting the text into the DOM. prepare(text, font, options) normalizes white space, finds break opportunities and measures segments once, returning an opaque handle; layout(handle, maxWidth, lineHeight) returns {height, lineCount}. prepareWithSegments() plus layoutWithLines(), walkLineRanges(), measureLineStats() and layoutNextLineRange() give line text, widths and cursors for drawing to Canvas or SVG, shrink-wrapping or flowing text around obstacles, and @chenglou/pretext/rich-inline handles mixed fonts, chips and inline boxes. It replaces reading offsetHeight or getBoundingClientRect, not the browser's painting: the caller still renders the text with matching CSS.
how_it_is_fast: A two-phase cache. prepare() runs ports of each engine's own line-break scan and grapheme rules (Blink, WebKit and Gecko tables pinned to browser builds, src/line-breaks.ts and src/gecko-line-breaks.ts), splits the text into break-delimited segments and measures each with Canvas measureText on an OffscreenCanvas, caching widths per (font, segment) in a shared Map. layout() is a greedy first-fit line walk over parallel arrays (widths as number[], segment kinds as a Uint8Array) with no Canvas calls, string work or per-line allocation; for plain prose a single numeric loop counts lines (the #338 fast path the CHANGELOG credits with a 2-3x faster layout() in Chrome and Safari). The range APIs return cursors instead of line strings, because the project found that most of the cost of getting lines was allocating strings and the GC that followed.
when_to_use: Virtualized lists, chat histories and feeds with thousands of text rows whose exact heights must be known before render and recomputed on every resize: prepare each message once, then call layout() per width (RESEARCH.md, before #338 and on a stand-in Canvas: 0.4-0.7 us per layout, 43-59 ms median to re-lay out 100,000 messages).

Userland layout that needs line geometry: masonry grids, chat bubbles shrink-wrapped to the widest line (walkLineRanges), text flowing around images (layoutNextLineRange), or drawing wrapped text into Canvas or SVG.
Code that would otherwise interleave DOM writes and reads across components and has to batch them to avoid layout thrashing.
Pre-sizing textarea-like pre-wrap text, or checking in development that labels do not wrap, in Chrome, Firefox and Safari 27 with named fonts and px sizes, including CJK, Arabic, Thai and emoji.
when_not_to_use: Measuring a text once: prepare() still calls Canvas measureText for every new segment, and nothing in the repo compares that cold cost with one DOM read; the gain comes from repeated layout() calls on cached widths.

Server-side rendering, Node or Bun without a Canvas, and React Native: it throws 'Text measurement requires OffscreenCanvas or a DOM canvas context.' (SSR #123 and React Native #131/#157 are open, server-side measurement is punted).

Pagination, print or any place where an undercount breaks the page: open #334 reports Songti SC 16px at 120 and 135 px giving 2 lines where Chrome gives 3, and #421 (2026-10-04) reports kerned overlong words ('AV', 'WAVE', 'To.') broken one letter off in Firefox 156, Chromium 147 and WebKit 26.4.

CSS outside its subset: system-ui or -apple-system on macOS, rem/em sizes, font-feature-settings or font-variation-settings, non-default font-kerning or word-spacing, hyphens: auto, word-break: break-all (#402), overflow-wrap: normal, bidi visual order, or per-span font sizes beyond what rich-inline models.
C or C++ code, or native apps: it is browser JavaScript tied to the host's Canvas text engine; for native shaping and layout see HarfBuzz-based stacks or Parley.

integration.form: module (npm @chenglou/pretext, ESM only, ships dist JS and TypeScript source; subpath export @chenglou/pretext/rich-inline)
integration.dependencies: none at runtime (devDependencies only); needs Canvas 2D measureText via OffscreenCanvas or a DOM canvas, Unicode property escapes, and Intl.Segmenter for Thai, Lao, Khmer, Myanmar and other Southeast Asian scripts
integration.min_toolchain: ES2018+ JavaScript engine with Unicode property escapes (a SyntaxError at load without them); built with TypeScript 6.0.2, developed with Bun; the WebKit profile follows Safari 27
integration.platforms: Browsers: Chrome/Edge (Blink), Firefox (Gecko), Safari 27 (WebKit); unrecognized engines get Blink's rules; works in Web Workers through OffscreenCanvas (emoji correction off there). Harness runs are on macOS (M5 Max) and an iOS simulator; Windows and Android are untested.
integration.thread_safety: Single-threaded JavaScript. One measurement context and the per-font segment-width cache are module globals per realm, so each worker has its own; setLocale() and clearCache() reset them for all later prepares. Prepared handles are not mutated by layout and copy through structuredClone() or postMessage().
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — replaces offsetHeight/getBoundingClientRect reads for paragraph height and line breaks only when the caller passes the same canvas font string, px line height and width as the CSS, and the text stays inside the supported CSS subset; the browser still paints the text.

gotchas: On main a JSON copy of a handle hangs: JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(prepared)) turns the Uint8Array segmentFlags into an object with no length, and the line APIs never return (CHANGELOG, #340); 0.0.9 tolerated it. Use structuredClone() or postMessage().

The shared per-font width cache grows with every new segment until clearCache() (TODO.md lists bounding it as open). After a web font finishes loading, call clearCache() and prepare again, or the cached widths stay those of the fallback font; the emoji correction also goes stale when zoom or devicePixelRatio crosses 1.25/1.5, leaving 4-5 px per emoji (#418).

Overlong words break between graphemes like overflow-wrap: break-word, which is not CSS's default, so set that property on the painted text; an empty string gives lineCount 0 where browsers size one line; a maxWidth that is NaN or undefined lays out as unbounded.

npm 'latest' is 0.0.9 (2026-09-07). Main carries a large unreleased section (engine ports #340, layout fast path #338, main bundle about 38 KB gzipped against 16 KB in 0.0.9), the maintainer holds releases until an API review, and license notices for the ported browser line-breaking code and engine data are not written yet (TODO.md), so check licensing before vendoring main.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: The other browser-JavaScript siblings (text-shaper, rustybuzz-wasm, Typr.js) parse fonts and shape glyphs themselves; Pretext does no shaping and instead predicts where the browser will wrap text it paints with its own font engine. Pick Pretext when the browser renders and app code needs heights or line breaks ahead of time; pick text-shaper or a HarfBuzz/Parley stack when you draw glyphs yourself or work outside a browser.
verified_claims_summary: No Pretext-versus-DOM measurement exists in the repo: bun harness bench times Pretext builds against each other in Chrome 154, Firefox 156.0.1 and Safari 27 on an M5 Max, and the only absolute figures are Pretext's own (chat demo on a stand-in Canvas: 46-100 us per first prepare, 0.4-0.7 us per layout; Chrome 153 prepared the corpora in 115 ms and Safari 26.5.2 in 350 ms on 2026-09-15; early npm READMEs: prepare about 19 ms and layout about 0.09 ms for 500 texts). The 300-600x, 500x and 540x figures come from third-party pages (one snippet: about 380 ms DOM versus 0.7 ms on 1,000 paragraphs), and per a search snippet the author called that comparison unfair because it sets a cached layout() against a cold DOM measurement.
status_note: Very active (1,511 commits on main, last commit 2026-10-03, 50.7k stars, 38 open issues) and MIT-licensed, but pre-1.0: the published 0.0.9 lags main by a month of engine rewrites, and the maintainer will not release before an API review.
